summary.prose: This Story makes everything the daemon runs follow the definitions: tier defaults, the summariser, the tool-loop model, the effort passed to a CLI, the CLI kind, Codex's input budget and Ollama's context window all come from the model registry, and an effort a model does not accept is dropped with a warning. A repo keeps only its choice of tier per role and its core floor; reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning, and models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx goes. The settings catalog builds its model defaults and effort values from the shipped definitions (imported as JSON, so the TUI, updater and VS Code bundle keep working); config.write refuses a rejected model and says when a restart is needed; models.resolveRole tells a client what the daemon would run; installers read their defaults from the file; and the embedder reads local settings only on first use.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The curated cloud catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381), as the DEF decided, and is extended in place; the boot hook moves ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads, because the settings defaults now come from the file. The file is extended into the model definitions: exactly one entry for each built-in family, each with its CLI kind (CLI families), its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model (CLI families), the Ollama tool-loop default, and the default family. Each Ollama model's input limit is its context window and replaces the global models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx; the output cap ollamaNumPredict stays global. A ModelRegistry built from the file and the per-user approved-model store answers every model question in the daemon; each thread builds it on first use and caches it, the way it loads and caches settings today (src/config/analyze.ts:234). A daemon restart guarantees that every thread uses a changed file, approval or saved tier; until then, a thread that starts or first reads them after the change, such as a worker the supervisor replaces after a crash (src/daemon/threads/supervisor.ts:136-148), may already use it, as with settings today. That is harmless: every saved tier has passed config.write's checks and every approval a check in which the model ran. The settings catalog takes the defaults of its tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows, and the allowed effort values, from the same file, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name stays in code. One read-only request, models.definitions, serves the definitions to clients and is the source of providers.listModels; models.resolveRole lets the TUI's review command run the model the daemon would. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs a tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor. Every Story leaves the build and tests passing, keeping a named stopgap for anything a later Story migrates. Settings-write safety is out of scope (ISSUE-8dc75bc5).

ownedContracts.name: Settings rules and models.resolveRole
ownedContracts.purpose: What changes in settings: the settings catalog's tier runner, tier model and local coreModel defaults and the allowed effort values come from the definitions; per-repo tier overrides are removed with a warning (k6, s3/ac5); ollamaNumCtx is pruned; config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model (s4/ac4) and reports restartRequired for model settings. models.resolveRole gives the TUI's review command the tier, model, effort and provider settings the daemon would use for a role and repo.

consumedContracts.name: ModelDefinitionsFile (the curated catalog file, extended)
consumedContracts.purpose: The shipped, versioned data format of src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json: the only place model facts and default model choices are stated (k4). Validated at daemon start (k7); a change applies at the next restart (s1/ac2). Ollama models must be listed to be selectable.

consumedContracts.name: ModelRegistry and the approved-model store
consumedContracts.purpose: The in-process view every daemon consumer asks, built from the sc1 file plus the per-user approved-model store and cached per thread like settings. Defines the store's entry shape (written by s4). Resolves aliases, accepted efforts, input limits and defaults, and applies decision A.

boundary.internal: Moving every daemon consumer onto the registry: tier resolution, summariser selection, effort forwarding, CliProvider's input budget and CLI kind, OllamaProvider's num_ctx, the tool-loop model (an unlisted coreModel runs the tool-loop default with a warning) and the runner and model literals in routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code; SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK, CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS and ollamaNumCtx go; DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS stop being written in code and remain only as temporary exports drawn from the definitions for the TUI's model-tiers pane, which s5 migrates; no daemon code uses them. The settings catalog's tier and coreModel defaults and effort values are taken from the definitions; how the settings catalog reaches the file is decided in this Story's LLD and must work in every process that loads the settings catalog today (the daemon, the TUI, the updater, and the VS Code bundle until s6 drops its use). Reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning and prunes ollamaNumCtx; readRepoOverride and its callers go. config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model and reports restartRequired. models.resolveRole and its method-class entry. Both installer copies take tier defaults and the tool-loop default from the file. Tests: an unset tier resolves to the file's default, and with a fixture whose defaults differ from today's, reconcile fills the fixture's values (ac1); an unsupported effort is dropped with a warning naming model and effort (ac2); a source scan fails on runner or model literals outside the family implementations, on any read of ollamaNumCtx, and on any daemon use of the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS exports (ac3); the TUI still builds and its model-tiers pane shows the definitions' defaults; a repo's `tasks` choice applies with the global tier's model (ac4); reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning naming repo and tier and keeps `tasks` and coreFloor (ac5); an unlisted model falls back with the warning (decision A); a fixture Ollama model's input limit sets num_ctx; config.write refuses a rejected model and reports restartRequired; models.resolveRole matches the daemon's own resolution for a CLI tier and an Ollama tier; the settings catalog loader accepts the catalog and an unset JetBrains tier still shows the default family's values.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Extending the catalog file, its types (CloudModelCatalogFile, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:48) and its validator in place; refreshing its contents with today's models, the aliases today's tier defaults use (opus, sonnet, haiku), the Ollama models insrc ships with and their context windows, and today's coreModel as the tool-loop default; the registry and its per-thread cache; moving the boot validation ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads; reading the approved-model store (a malformed store is logged and treated as empty); keeping the curated catalog's existing accessor answering providers.listModels from the new file shape until s2 replaces it. The validator refuses a missing or malformed file, an unknown, missing or repeated family, a CLI family without its CLI kind, tier defaults or summariser model, a model without an efforts list, a duplicate id or alias, a default that is not a model of its family, an Ollama model without a token input limit, and a tool-loop default that is not listed, naming the entry (ac3). Tests: one fixture per refusal reason (ac3); a model and alias added to a fixture are served after a restart with no code change (ac2); the file is validated before the settings reconcile, before any worker starts and before listen (ac1, k7); repeated requests in one thread return the same definitions even after the file changes on disk (ac1); a replacement worker started after the file, the store or config.json changed on disk uses the new values while a surviving thread keeps its own until the restart, and a thread whose first read comes after such a change likewise uses the new values; after a daemon restart every thread resolves the same definitions, approvals and tiers; providers.listModels still returns today's Claude and Codex models through the kept accessor; alias, effort and limit lookups; resolveTier distinguishes rejected-model from unlisted-model and falls back to the tier's family default, or the default family's for an Ollama tier.

The models.definitions handler and its method-class entry, the projection of the registry, each listed Ollama model's installed state from the existing bounded listing, and re-sourcing providers.listModels from the registry (for Ollama, listed models only), then removing the curated catalog accessor s1 kept. Tests: models.definitions returns every field of a fixture file (ac1); providers.listModels and models.definitions agree for every family, and an installed but unlisted Ollama model appears in neither (ac2); with Ollama not answering, installed is absent and the request still succeeds.

The per-family check procedures (Codex: the CLI's model list plus a run; Claude: a run, the input limit from the JSON output, recognised effort names), run one call at a time; telling a reachable CLI that refuses the model apart from an unreachable CLI; refusing approval unless the model ran without error; writing the store atomically and acknowledging a decision only once it is written; the method-class entries. Tests: checks against fake CLIs record each verdict and run one at a time (ac1); results list each claimed level with evidence and nothing is usable before approval (ac2); after approval and a restart only the approved levels are accepted (ac3); a rejected profile or unreachable CLI refuses the model with a reason, and approving a check whose model did not run is refused (ac4); after a restart an approved model appears in models.definitions as user-approved and a rejected one among the rejected ids (ac5); a failed store write returns write-failed and keeps the previous store.

The TUI model-tiers pane and its effort choices from models.definitions, removing the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS exports s3 kept; the unknown-model check and approval screen; the repo settings view limited to `tasks` and coreFloor; showing restartRequired and offering maintenance.restart; the review command using models.resolveRole and building its provider from the answer instead of reading config.json; Setup recommending the definitions' tool-loop default instead of DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL, and saying it cannot recommend when the daemon is not running. Tests: the pane offers exactly the options of a fake models.definitions answer and no source file still exports or imports DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS (ac1); saving an unknown model starts the check and shows its results (ac2); the repo view edits only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3); the review command runs the model a fake models.resolveRole returns for a CLI and an Ollama tier; Setup recommends the fake answer's tool-loop default.

The VS Code model-tier picker driven by models.definitions instead of its runner list and the bundled settings catalog's effort rows, removing the bundle's import of the settings catalog; the unknown-model check and approval prompt; the Repo Configuration panel without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired and offering insrc.daemon.restart. Tests: the picker offers exactly a fake answer's options and the bundle keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the repo panel shows only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

The JetBrains model-tiers section driven by models.definitions instead of ModelTiersModel.PROVIDERS; the unknown-model check and approval dialog; the per-repo settings without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired. Tests: the section offers exactly a fake answer's options and the plugin keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the per-repo settings show only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — daemon serves and runs by the definitions

nonFunctional.performance: The file is parsed once per thread and every model question is an in-memory lookup; models.definitions touches no CLI and makes one bounded Ollama listing call, the same one providers.listModels makes today.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud REST call is added (k1): checks run only through the installed claude and codex CLIs. The approved-model store is a per-user file under the insrc home written only by the daemon; clients reach it only through models.approve and models.reject (k2).
nonFunctional.observability: A bad file stops the daemon with a log naming the entry (s1/ac3); a dropped effort logs model and effort (s3/ac2); a tier fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A); a tool-loop substitution logs both models; removing a per-repo tier override logs repo and tier (s3/ac5); each CLI call of a check and its verdict is logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Approved and rejected profiles live outside the shipped file and config.json, so they survive restarts and updates; the store is replaced atomically and a decision is acknowledged only once written; a malformed store is logged and treated as empty. When an update ships a model the user had approved, the shipped definition wins. Existing `tasks`, coreFloor, ollamaNumPredict and every tier value already in config.json are kept. Between a change and the next restart, threads may differ (a replaced worker or a late first read uses the new values); the restart brings them together.

api.name: config.write
api.signature: 'config.write': (params: { path: string | string[]; value: unknown }) => Promise<ConfigWriteResult>  // ConfigWriteResult = { ok: true; restartRequired?: boolean } | { ok: false; reason?: 'invalid-path' | 'rejected-model'; detail?: string }

returns.meaning: ok:true, with restartRequired:true when the path is under models.tiers, models.tasks, models.coreFloor, models.byRepo or is models.local.coreModel; ok:false with reason 'invalid-path' (as today) or 'rejected-model' with a detail naming the model and family.

errors.condition: The path is models.tiers.<tier>.model and the value is an effective rejected id of the family that tier's runner names (the runner after the write; for an ollama runner nothing is rejected). config.json is not written.
Empty path or empty segment, as today.

preconditions: The daemon has validated the definitions at boot.
postconditions: A refused write leaves config.json unchanged.
Other paths behave as today (settings-write safety is ISSUE-8dc75bc5, out of scope).

api.name: models.resolveRole
api.signature: 'models.resolveRole': (params: { role: string; repoPath: string }) => Promise<RoleResolution | { error: string; recoverable: false }>  // RoleResolution as HLD sc5

parameters.name: params
parameters.purpose: The reasoning role and the repo whose `tasks`/coreFloor apply.

returns.meaning: The tier (after the repo's/global tasks and the core floor), family, canonical model id, the effort that will be passed, the model's inputLimit, the decision-A fallback when one happened, cli.kind for a CLI family, and for ollama the host, numCtx (the model's token limit) and the global numPredict — exactly what the daemon's own router uses.

errors.condition: role or repoPath missing or not a string.

preconditions: Registered in buildHandlerRuntime and the method-class table as a session method.
postconditions: Read-only; builds no provider and runs no model.

api.name: resolveTier
api.signature: resolveTier(tiering: TieringOverride, tier: TierName): TierModel  // src/config/analyze.ts; TierModel.effort is EffortLevel

returns.meaning: getModelRegistry().resolveTier(tier, configured-or-default setting) mapped to { runner: family, model: canonical id, effort? }; an unset tier uses the default family's tierDefault (ac1).

preconditions: Runs in a daemon thread (the registry is available).
postconditions: A droppedEffort logs a warning naming tier, model and effort and is never forwarded (ac2).
A fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A).

api.name: resolveRole
api.signature: resolveRole(role: RoleId, cfg: AnalyzeConfig, repoPath: string | undefined, deps?: RoleRouterDeps): RoleResolution  // src/analyze/context/role-router.ts

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Selects the repo's `tasks` and coreFloor only.

returns.meaning: Tier from byRepo tasks → global tasks → taxonomy default, clamped by the core floor (byRepo ?? global); runner, model and effort only from the resolved global tier (ac4); no byRepo.tiers layer and no DEFAULT_TIERS fallback.

preconditions: cfg comes from loadAnalyzeConfig (tiers already resolved through the registry).
postconditions: The legacy per-repo shaper override (deps.repoOverride from resolveRepoShaperProvider) no longer exists; clientDefault and the explicit global runner keep their existing roles.

api.name: buildShaperProvider
api.signature: buildShaperProvider(cfg: AnalyzeConfig, overrides?: ShaperProviderOverrides): LLMProvider  // and buildSummariserProvider(cfg): LLMProvider

returns.meaning: For a CLI family: CliProvider with kind = registry.cliKind(family), the canonical model, the effort only when the resolved model accepts it, and inputBudgetChars = the model's inputLimit.max when its unit is 'chars'. For ollama: OllamaProvider with num_ctx = the model's token inputLimit. The summariser uses registry.summariserModel(family) when the cheap tier's model is not a model of its family (replacing SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK).

postconditions: SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK and the cli-claude/cli-codex → claude/codex literal mapping are gone; resolveShaperKind's final floor is the default family's tier runner rather than a literal.

api.name: localToolLoopModel
api.signature: localToolLoopModel(cfg: AnalyzeConfig): { model: string; numCtx: number }  // src/analyze/context/driver.ts

returns.meaning: The configured models.local.coreModel when the ollama family lists it, else registry.toolLoopModel() with a warning naming both; numCtx is that model's token inputLimit (replacing cfg.shaper.ollamaNumCtx).

api.name: CONFIG_CATALOG
api.signature: export const CONFIG_CATALOG: readonly ConfigOption[]  // = buildConfigCatalog(SHIPPED_DEFINITIONS); export function buildConfigCatalog(defs: ModelDefinitionsFile): readonly ConfigOption[]

returns.meaning: Rows unchanged except: models.tiers.<tier>.runner default = defs.defaultFamily and enumValues = the family ids; models.tiers.<tier>.model default = that family's tierDefaults[tier].model; models.tiers.<tier>.effort enumValues = '' plus the de-duplicated efforts of the shipped models; models.local.coreModel default = the ollama toolLoopModel; models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx removed (and added to RETIRED_PATHS).

preconditions: SHIPPED_DEFINITIONS is the shipped file imported as a JSON module (resolveJsonModule + `with { type: 'json' }`); tsc rejects a syntactically broken file at build.
postconditions: The daemon reconciles with buildConfigCatalog(validateModelCatalog()) (validated, test-seamed); the TUI, the updater's loadBuiltCatalog and the VS Code bundle use CONFIG_CATALOG from the shipped JSON.

api.name: reconcileConfig
api.signature: reconcileConfig(config: unknown, catalog?: readonly ConfigOption[], retired?: readonly RetiredPath[]): ConfigReconcileResult

returns.meaning: As today, plus: every models.byRepo[repo].tiers subtree is removed and reported in `pruned` as models.byRepo["<repo>"].tiers.<tier> for each tier it held; tasks and coreFloor are kept; models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx is pruned as a retired path.

postconditions: The boot reconcile logs one warning per removed per-repo tier naming repo and tier (ac5).

api.name: CliProvider
api.signature: new CliProvider(opts: { kind: 'claude' | 'codex'; model?: string; effort?: EffortLevel; inputBudgetChars?: number; timeoutMs?: number })

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: kind and model from the registry; effort only when accepted; inputBudgetChars from the model's chars limit.

returns.meaning: inputBudgetChars comes from opts instead of CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS (removed); effort typed EffortLevel.

postconditions: The family implementation keeps its own 'claude' | 'codex' flag mapping (it is the family implementation).

api.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
api.signature: embeddingModel(): string; embeddingDim(): number  // src/indexer/embedder.ts: the module-load EMBEDDING_MODEL / EMBEDDING_DIM constants become first-use getters

returns.meaning: loadLocalProviderConfig() is called on first use, not at module load (HLD override item 1); embedding values themselves are unchanged and out of scope (override item 3).

postconditions: Importing src/daemon/index.ts reads no local settings before main() validates the definitions.

errorCases.scenario: A tier is set to an effort its model does not accept (for example 'ultra' on gpt-6-luna, or any effort on an Ollama model).
errorCases.detection: getModelRegistry().resolveTier returns droppedEffort when loadAnalyzeConfig resolves the tier.
errorCases.response: Logs a warning naming tier, model and effort once per thread (when the config is assembled) and builds the provider without an effort.
errorCases.userImpact: The CLI runs at its own default effort; the log says why (ac2).

errorCases.scenario: A tier is set to a model its family neither lists nor has approved, or one the user rejected.
errorCases.response: Logs a warning naming tier, requested model, reason and the default used, and runs the tier default (decision A).
errorCases.userImpact: Work continues on the default model; the setting is left as written for the user to fix.

errorCases.scenario: models.local.coreModel names an Ollama model the definitions do not list.
errorCases.detection: registry.find('ollama', coreModel) returns undefined in localToolLoopModel.
errorCases.response: Uses registry.toolLoopModel() and logs a warning naming both models.
errorCases.userImpact: The tool loop runs on the listed default.

errorCases.scenario: config.write sets models.tiers.<tier>.model to a model the user rejected.
errorCases.detection: The handler resolves the tier's runner after the write and checks registry.rejected(family).includes(value).
errorCases.response: Returns { ok:false, reason:'rejected-model', detail } and leaves config.json untouched.
errorCases.userImpact: The client shows the refusal (s5-s7 render it).

errorCases.scenario: models.resolveRole is called without a string role or repoPath.
errorCases.detection: Parameter check at the top of the handler.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller gets the standard error envelope.

errorCases.scenario: The installer cannot read the definitions file (missing or not JSON) in step 4b.
errorCases.response: The installer stops with an error naming the file (the build in step 3 would already have failed for a broken file).
errorCases.userImpact: Installation does not write a config with guessed models.

edgeCases.expected: Resolves to the default family's tierDefault for that tier, with that default's effort (ac1).
Resolves to the canonical model (claude-opus-5-5); provider gets the canonical id.

edgeCases.expected: Reconcile removes byRepo tiers with a warning naming repo and tier; the role runs on the GLOBAL cheap tier's runner and model (ac4, ac5).
Pruned by reconcile as a retired path; no code reads it.

edgeCases.input: A config whose tiers.core.model is '' (today's default).
edgeCases.expected: Treated as unset: resolves to the definitions' core default.

edgeCases.input: An effort the user's approved model accepts but no shipped model lists.
edgeCases.expected: Accepted at resolution (the registry includes approved efforts); the catalog's effort enum (shipped efforts only) does not limit config.write, which does not enum-check.

edgeCases.input: The cheap tier runs on ollama.
edgeCases.expected: The summariser builds an OllamaProvider with num_ctx from the model's token inputLimit.
CliProvider gets no inputBudgetChars (only a 'chars' limit sets it), as today.

invariantsToPreserve.text: loadAnalyzeConfig stays per-thread cached and fail-soft: a malformed config.json still yields defaults with a warning, now the definitions' defaults.

The role router keeps its precedence for the tier (byRepo tasks → global tasks → taxonomy) and the core-floor clamp (byRepo coreFloor ?? global), and keeps the global tier's effort for every routed role.
CliProvider forwards an effort exactly as today: claude --effort <e>, codex -c model_reasoning_effort=<e>; no effort when none is set.
Every process that loads the settings catalog (daemon reconcile, TUI, updater via loadBuiltCatalog, VS Code bundle) keeps loading it.
Reconcile keeps models.tasks, models.coreFloor and each byRepo entry's tasks and coreFloor, and still reports changes in carried/filled/repaired/pruned.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test via tsx (npx tsx --test), as src/config/__tests__/tier-defaults.test.ts, src/daemon/__tests__/config-boot-reconcile.test.ts and src/agent/providers/__tests__/cli-subprocess.test.ts

testLevels.purpose: Tier resolution, routing, provider construction, settings catalog and reconcile against fixture definitions.
subjects: tier resolution (src/config/analyze.ts): an unset tier resolves to the fixture definitions' default with its effort; a tier set by alias resolves to the canonical model; '' model is unset
effort: a tier whose model does not accept its effort resolves without it and logs a warning naming tier, model and effort; the built CliProvider gets no effort
decision A: an unlisted and a rejected model fall back to the tier default with a warning naming tier, requested model, reason and default
role router (src/analyze/context/role-router.ts): a repo's tasks choice picks the tier while runner, model and effort come from the global tier; byRepo coreFloor still clamps

provider construction: CLI kind from registry.cliKind; Codex inputBudgetChars from the model's chars limit; haiku gets none; an Ollama tier's num_ctx is the fixture model's token limit; the summariser uses the family's summariserModel when the cheap model is not of its family
tool loop: a listed coreModel is used with its token limit; an unlisted coreModel runs registry.toolLoopModel() with a warning naming both

settings catalog: buildConfigCatalog(fixture) gives tier runner/model defaults, effort enum values and coreModel default from the fixture; CONFIG_CATALOG equals buildConfigCatalog(shipped); no ollamaNumCtx row; loadBuiltCatalog accepts the built catalog

reconcile: with a fixture whose defaults differ from today's, a fresh config is filled with the fixture's values; byRepo tiers are removed and reported per repo and tier, tasks and coreFloor kept; models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx pruned

config.write: a rejected tier model is refused with reason 'rejected-model' and config.json unchanged; a tier, tasks, coreFloor or coreModel write returns restartRequired:true; an unrelated write does not
models.resolveRole: for a CLI tier and an Ollama tier the answer equals the router's resolution and the provider settings the daemon builds; bad params give the invalid-params error
embedder: importing src/indexer/embedder.ts does not call loadLocalProviderConfig; the first getter call does

migration.stateBefore: Tier defaults are literals (DEFAULT_TIERS cli-claude opus/sonnet/haiku, src/config/analyze.ts:134) and resolution never consults the definitions (src/config/analyze.ts:252); efforts are limited to TIER_EFFORTS and forwarded unchecked (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:530); per-repo tiers override global tiers in the router (src/analyze/context/role-router.ts:138) and as a fresh per-repo shaper override (src/daemon/code-review-rpc.ts:194, src/daemon/workflow-rpc.ts:422); the summariser falls back to literal CLI models (src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:271); Codex's budget is CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:181); Ollama runs at models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx (src/config/analyze.ts:222) and the tool loop at local.coreModel unchecked (src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1106); the settings catalog and both installers hold model literals (src/config/config-catalog.ts:113-142, scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh:275-324); the embedder reads local settings at module load (src/indexer/embedder.ts:16).
migration.stateAfter: Every daemon model choice resolves through the registry: tier defaults, efforts (unaccepted ones dropped with a warning), decision-A fallbacks, CLI kind, Codex budget (from the file's chars limit), Ollama num_ctx (from the model's token limit), the summariser and the tool-loop model. A repo chooses only its tier per role and core floor. The settings catalog builds its model defaults and effort values from the shipped JSON; reconcile removes per-repo tiers and ollamaNumCtx with warnings; config.write refuses rejected models and reports restartRequired; models.resolveRole answers what the daemon would run; installers read defaults from the file; the embedder reads settings on first use. DEFAULT_TIERS/TIER_EFFORTS remain only as JSON-derived exports for the TUI pane until s5.

An empty core model ('' today) now resolves to the definitions' core default (opus), the model the claude CLI chose by default. config.write's result gains optional fields (restartRequired, reason, detail), so existing clients that read only ok keep working; models.resolveRole is new. alternativesConsidered.name: Catalog built from the definitions by a JSON import; daemon resolution through the registry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: config-catalog.ts builds its model rows from the shipped definitions imported as JSON (works in daemon, TUI, updater and the VS Code bundle); every daemon consumer resolves through getModelRegistry().
alternativesConsidered.approach: Settings catalog: src/config/config-catalog.ts imports the shipped definitions file as a JSON module (import attributes, resolveJsonModule) and exports buildConfigCatalog(defs) plus CONFIG_CATALOG = buildConfigCatalog(shipped). The tier runner default is defaultFamily, each tier model default is that family's tierDefaults[tier].model, the effort enum is '' plus the efforts of the shipped models, and models.local.coreModel defaults to the Ollama toolLoopModel; models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx leaves the catalog and joins RETIRED_PATHS. tsc emits and copy-assets ships the JSON beside out/config, so the updater's import of out/config/config-catalog.js and the esbuild VS Code bundle both resolve it; the daemon's reconcile uses buildConfigCatalog(validateModelCatalog()) so the validated (and test-seamed) file is the one reconciled. Resolution: loadAnalyzeConfig resolves each global tier with getModelRegistry().resolveTier and logs droppedEffort and fallback (decision A); TierModel.effort becomes EffortLevel; byRepo parsing keeps only tasks and coreFloor; the role router takes the tier from byRepo/global tasks and the model only from the global tiers; buildShaperProvider/buildSummariserProvider take the CLI kind from registry.cliKind, CliProvider takes its input budget and accepted effort from the resolved model, OllamaProvider its num_ctx from the model's inputLimit, the tool-loop model from the configured coreModel when listed or registry.toolLoopModel() with a warning; readRepoOverride and resolveRepoShaperProvider/Model go. Reconcile removes models.byRepo[repo].tiers with a warning naming repo and tier. config.write refuses a tier model in registry.rejected and returns restartRequired for models.tiers/models.local paths. models.resolveRole wraps the router's pure resolution. DEFAULT_TIERS/TIER_EFFORTS are derived from the shipped JSON for the TUI only. The embedder reads local settings on first use. Installers read tier and tool-loop defaults from the cloned file with node.
pros: One source for defaults in every process that loads the catalog, including the bundled VS Code extension, without a runtime file path.
The daemon reconciles from the validated file and tests can drive reconcile with a fixture.
Reuses the registry's resolveTier, cliKind, toolLoopModel and rejected() rather than re-deriving them.
cons: Needs resolveJsonModule and an import attribute in tsconfig/config-catalog.ts; the JSON travels inside the VS Code bundle until s6 drops its catalog use.
Outside the daemon the catalog's defaults come from the shipped file unvalidated (the daemon validates at boot).

alternativesConsidered.name: Catalog reads the file from a path beside the module
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: config-catalog.ts reads the definitions with readFileSync from a path relative to import.meta.url at module load; resolution as in a1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same resolution and settings changes as a1, but CONFIG_CATALOG's model rows come from reading out/assets/models (or src/assets/models under tsx) relative to the module file at load time.
pros: No tsconfig change; the same file path the daemon validates.
cons: Breaks the VS Code bundle (esbuild output has no asset beside it) until s6, which the HLD requires to keep working.
A file read at module load in every process importing the catalog, including the TUI and the updater's dynamic import.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same resolution as a1 but violates sc5 by breaking the VS Code bundle's catalog.

cons: Model names stay as literals in code (violates k4 and ac3) and the TUI, updater and VS Code bundle see the literal defaults.
